sections.name: TotpService (RFC 6238 TOTP Engine) (part 1)
sections.title: Tests for codes, links and setup
sections.what: Checks that a secret can be converted to text and back without loss, that generated codes are six digits and accepted within a short time window, that wrong or malformed codes are refused, and that the setup link for authenticator apps has the expected format.
sections.why: Likely reason: these are the everyday behaviours a user would notice in two-factor sign-in, so they are checked first.
sections.watch_out: The window test relies on the service accepting codes from a neighbouring time step, so changing the window size can break it.

sections.name: TotpService (RFC 6238 TOTP Engine) (part 2)
sections.title: Official test values and encryption checks
sections.what: Compares the service's output with the published test values from RFC 6238 at several points in time, then checks that a stored secret is encrypted and decrypts back to the original. It also begins a check that the service refuses to start in production without an encryption key.
sections.why: Likely reason: the published test values prove the code math matches the standard that authenticator apps follow.
sections.watch_out: The published values only hold if the step length and digit count stay the same, so changing either setting will make these tests fail.

sections.name: TotpService (RFC 6238 TOTP Engine) (part 3)
sections.title: Replay check and backup code tests
sections.what: Confirms that the production refusal message appears when the key is missing. It then simulates a rule that a used time step must not be accepted again, and checks that a backup code works once and cannot be reused.
sections.why: Likely reason: reusing a code is a known attack, so the test documents the rule even though the check is written inside the test itself.
sections.watch_out: The replay part does not call the real service logic. It only proves the simulated rule, so it does not prove the app blocks reuse.
